children: , the enterprise cybersecurity company, launched a worldwide annual subscription that puts Unit 42's security testing on a continuous cycle. Shares rose about 3.45% to $387.485 Wednesday morning. The pitch is straightforward: find a weakness, check whether an attacker could use it, then help the customer fix it.

The service draws on Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5, OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber and open-weight models. Palo Alto says it can test applications, APIs, cloud systems, code and networks, then prioritize fixes and recommend virtual patches. The distinction is whether those tests lead to fewer openings for attackers, rather than a longer list of alerts.

At $387.485, the shares stood 66.17% above the $233.18 GF Value shown for September 23. That is a demanding price for a new subscription service. Annual contracts could make Unit 42's revenue steadier, but model usage and specialist work have costs. Renewals, customer results and margins will show whether this launch earns its place in the valuation.

title: Palo Alto Jumps 3.5% as AI Pen Testing Becomes a Subscription
